incidents.victim: Enterprise networks using Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE)
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated crafted HTTP request exploits authentication bypass in Cisco ISE API endpoint (CVE-2026-76460, CVSS 10.0), granting root-level access without credentials.
incidents.impact: Attackers gain control of ISE — the hub of most enterprise network access controls — enabling them to disable defenses, impersonate hosts, and pivot freely across connected networks; CISA added to KEV catalog same day patches released.

incidents.victim: IT professionals and cryptocurrency firms — Japan, US, Europe, globally
incidents.vector: Fake job interview campaigns distributing malicious NPM packages (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, StoatWaffle) via social media and freelance platforms to compromise developer devices.
incidents.impact: 30,000+ devices infected across 100 countries; $10.7M stolen from 7,000+ cryptocurrency wallets; Japan's first laptop farm dismantled; North Korean IT workers simultaneously infiltrating tech companies via stolen identities.

incidents.victim: US frontier AI model developers
incidents.vector: Industrial-scale systematic querying of US frontier AI models to extract proprietary model capabilities and training methodology through knowledge distillation at scale.
incidents.impact: Intellectual property extracted from US AI companies, eroding US competitive advantage in frontier AI development; CISA, NSA, and FBI issued joint advisory with TTPs and defensive guidance.

incidents.victim: Russian technology and defense sector companies
incidents.vector: Stolen VPN credentials used to access corporate networks; GhostContainer memory-only backdoor deployed via Microsoft Exchange server manipulation to evade security logging.
incidents.impact: Multiple Russian companies breached; domain controllers targeted for persistent access; group previously focused on Chinese high-tech and defense sector has expanded scope to Russian targets.

incidents.victim: 12+ companies — entertainment, telecom, technology, cloud, cryptocurrency (US)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — social engineering and data extortion
incidents.vector: Social engineering via phone calls impersonating IT support to steal employee credentials; SIM swapping to hijack accounts of high-net-worth cryptocurrency holders.
incidents.impact: Ahmed Elbadawy pleaded guilty; ~$17.6M in cryptocurrency, vehicles, jewelry and designer goods sought for forfeiture; 29 individuals and 12+ companies victimized between 2021–2023.

incidents.victim: Dissidents, activists, journalists — UK, US, Netherlands, worldwide
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing via WhatsApp and Telegram impersonating trusted contacts, tricking targets into installing CHOSEN BRICK malware disguised as apps (Pictory, Norton, KeePass) or fake medical files.
incidents.impact: Device compromise enabling collection of emails, messages, contacts, screen captures, and microphone audio; personal data published on pro-Iranian leak sites enabling tracking of movements and potential physical targeting of dissidents abroad.

incidents.victim: Unnamed Spanish organization
incidents.vector: AI agent (LLM) autonomously discovered loose credentials via open-source intelligence, then chained them with a corporate application vulnerability to access personal data systems.
incidents.impact: Personal data records modified; corporate invoices accessed; Spain's data protection authority (AEPD) published it as the first confirmed agentic AI-enabled breach on record.

incidents.victim: Veradigm (Electronic Health Records platform)
incidents.vector: Third-party vendor compromise provided attackers with a foothold into Veradigm's healthcare network.
incidents.impact: Patient and provider data breach disclosed in SEC filing; scope of exposure under investigation; EHR systems serving thousands of clinicians potentially affected.

incidents.victim: Trezor hardware wallet users
incidents.vector: Breach of Trezor's third-party email service provider; phishing emails sent from official Trezor domain accounts to hardware wallet customers.
incidents.impact: Official Trezor accounts weaponized to deliver phishing to cryptocurrency users; campaign designed to steal wallet credentials, seed phrases, and private keys.

incidents.victim: Stadtwerke Landsberg KU (German public utility)
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack targeting corporate and business IT infrastructure at a German municipal utility provider.
incidents.impact: Corporate and business IT systems encrypted; public utility services (electricity, gas, water) unaffected; incident response and recovery ongoing.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center
incidents.vector: Exploitation of Cisco Secure FMC authentication bypass (CVE-2026-20079, CVSS 10.0) and static credential flaw (CVE-2026-20316) to deploy Cyclops Blink persistent backdoor across managed firewall networks.
incidents.impact: Cyclops Blink malware deployed with DNS-over-HTTPS C2 channels; managed device configurations and credentials harvested for lateral movement into connected enterprise networks; active espionage campaign ongoing.

incidents.victim: Undisclosed enterprise — Cisco FMC ransomware victim
incidents.vector: Logged into Cisco Secure FMC using static default credentials (CVE-2026-20316); performed full Active Directory reconnaissance and mass credential harvesting before deploying Qilin ransomware to selected endpoints.
incidents.impact: Active Directory architecture fully mapped; enterprise credentials stolen; Qilin ransomware deployed causing significant data encryption across the organization.

incidents.victim: Windows users and enterprises globally
incidents.vector: Active in-the-wild exploitation of Windows privilege escalation zero-days CVE-2026-81963 (Update Stack) and CVE-2026-85880 (ALPC heap overflow) before September Patch Tuesday.
incidents.impact: Privilege escalation to SYSTEM on vulnerable Windows machines; Microsoft's largest-ever single patch batch (974 vulnerabilities, 113 critical) released; both zero-days confirmed actively exploited prior to patches.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government organization (unnamed)
incidents.vector: ClearFake JavaScript injected on a compromised website displayed a ClickFix CAPTCHA that prompted the target to execute a WebDAV DLL loader, installing Amatera credential stealer and NetSupport Manager RAT.
incidents.impact: Credentials harvested from Ukrainian government network; persistent remote access established via NetSupport Manager with command-and-control infrastructure based in Russia.

incidents.victim: Berlin city government (Germany)
incidents.vector: Employee infected via ClickFix fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA prompt that triggered malware installation; Rhysida ransomware subsequently deployed to city government systems.
incidents.impact: $2 million ransom demanded; Berlin officials refused to pay; sensitive government data published on Rhysida ransomware group's data leak site.

incidents.victim: French notary sector — 500+ offices (~7% of all French notaries)
incidents.vector: Phishing campaigns to gain persistent deep network access; wire transaction details silently modified over years to redirect notarial property transaction payments.
incidents.impact: €35 million stolen over 4 years from 500+ notary offices; ANSSI spent 2 years on remediation; risk of forged notarized documents identified; French notary sector now mandating 2FA for financial transactions.

incidents.victim: Liquid Network (Blockstream cryptocurrency platform)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an undisclosed vulnerability in the Liquid Network cryptocurrency settlement platform protocol.
incidents.impact: $320 million in Bitcoin extracted; platform suspended; attackers claiming 'white hat' status returned ~$273M but retained ~$47M as a self-declared bug bounty.

incidents.victim: IDScan — 153 million US and Canadian citizens
incidents.vector: Long-term unauthorized access to IDScan identity verification systems; driver's license data continuously exfiltrated for over a year and sold via the 'Nexus' dark web service.
incidents.impact: 153 million US and Canadian driver's licenses exposed (~63% of all US licenses), including senior federal officials; database growing ~400,000 records daily; national security implications acknowledged; class-action lawsuits filed.

incidents.victim: Two private water utilities in Colorado (US)
incidents.vector: Remote access to operational technology equipment controlling water distribution systems at two privately-owned Colorado utilities serving under 200 customers each.
incidents.impact: Water system equipment remotely manipulated; Colorado governor confirmed incidents; no impact on public safety or water service reported; incidents under federal investigation.

incidents.victim: JetBrains Cadence customers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of vulnerability in JetBrains' own TeamCity CI/CD servers; attackers pivoted to the Cadence cloud-based LLM training platform used by customers.
incidents.impact: Source code and credentials stored by customers in Cadence LLM training instances likely stolen; software and AI development intellectual property compromised.
